items.text: Lose ten dollars, and you still buy the ticket. Lose the ticket, and you don't. Lost a ten-dollar bill on the way to the theater? Eighty-eight percent still bought a ticket. Lost the ten-dollar ticket itself? Only forty-six percent bought another. Same money. But your brain says the show now costs twenty. So:

Make the cheap chocolate free, and people stop buying the fancy one. Researchers sold a fancy truffle for fifteen cents, a cheap chocolate for one. Most bought the truffle.
